rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
$$\text{Particles per cell: corner }\frac{1}{8},\ \text{edge }\frac{1}{4},\ \text{face }\frac{1}{2},\ \text{body }1$$
$$\text{SC: }a=2r,\ Z=1,\ 52.4\%;\quad \text{BCC: }\sqrt{3}a=4r,\ Z=2,\ 68\%;\quad \text{FCC: }\sqrt{2}a=4r,\ Z=4,\ 74\%$$
$$\rho=\frac{ZM}{a^{3}N_{A}},\qquad n\lambda=2d\sin\theta\ (\text{Bragg})$$

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ A unit cell is the same as a crystal lattice. ✅ The lattice is the array of points; the unit cell is the smallest repeating block of that lattice with its contents.  ·  ❌ A corner atom belongs entirely to one unit cell. ✅ It is shared by eight cells, so it contributes only 1/8.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Seven crystal systems combine with four centering types to give 14 Bravais lattices.  ·  Coordination numbers: simple cubic 6, BCC 8, FCC (and HCP) 12.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Problem:** Copper (FCC, a = 361 pm, M = 63.5 g mol⁻¹) — find the density. **Solution:** Z = 4; ρ = ZM/(a³N_A) = (4 × 63.5)/((3.61×10⁻⁸ cm)³ × 6.022×10²³) ≈ 8.97 g cm⁻³, matching the known value for copper.  ·  **Problem:** Show that the radius of an atom in a BCC lattice is r = √3a/4. **Solution:** along the body diagonal of length √3a, the atoms touch: √3a = 4r, hence r = √3a/4 ≈ 0.433a.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: introduction to unit crystal lattice, unit cell (within States of Matter).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Meaning  ·  A **crystal lattice** is the regular three-dimensional arrangement of points (lattice points) in space at which the constituent particles of a crystal lie. A **unit cell** is the smallest repeating portion of that lattice which, when repeated in three dimensions, generates the whole crystal — it is the building block or 'brick' of the crystal. Lattice + the atoms/ions/molecules at its points = the crystal structure.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Polonium is the standard 'real-life' example of a simple cubic metal; NaCl crystallises in a face-centred cubic array of ions.  ·  answer pattern for "Introduction to unit crystal lattice and unit cell": define → method → result. Structure earns the marks on 6–10 mark questions.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 2. Lattice parameters and crystal systems  ·  A unit cell is described by six parameters: the three edge lengths a, b, c and the three interaxial angles α, β, γ. Depending on their relative values, crystals fall into **7 crystal systems** (cubic, tetragonal, orthorhombic, monoclinic, triclinic, hexagonal and rhombohedral) which give **14 Bravais lattices** when the four possible cell centreings are included.  ·  ### 3. Types of unit cell

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ BCC and FCC have the same number of atoms per cell. ✅ BCC has Z = 2, FCC has Z = 4 and simple cubic Z = 1.  ·  ❌ The closest packing of equal spheres reaches 100%. ✅ The maximum (FCC/HCP) is 74%; simple cubic reaches only 52.4%.  ·  ❌ Unit cell dimensions cannot be measured. ✅ They are measured routinely from X-ray diffraction patterns using Bragg's law.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: For any structural question, identify the lattice type first, then the values Z, r and packing efficiency follow.  ·  List the seven crystal systems and state the relationship between the number of Bravais lattices and them.  ·  Calculate the number of atoms per unit cell for simple cubic, BCC and FCC lattices, showing the share of corner, face and body-centre particles.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Derive the relation between edge length and atomic radius for BCC and FCC cells.  ·  The edge length of a FCC unit cell of copper is 361 pm; calculate the density of copper (M = 63.5 g mol⁻¹).  ·  State the limitations of the ideal unit-cell model.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: • **Primitive (simple) cell:** particles only at the eight corners.  ·  • **Body-centred cell (BCC):** corners + one particle at the body centre.  ·  • **Face-centred cell (FCC):** corners + one particle at the centre of each of the six faces.
